title.narrative: EMPOWER-Jordan: Enabling and Mobilizing Civil Society Organisations in Jordan through Reinforced Institutional Advocacy and Technical Capacities to Enhance Coordination for Sustainable Developmen

description.narrative:
This action is in line with the overall objective of the call for proposals, which is to contribute to an inclusive, participatory, empowered, and independent civil society in Jordan as well as an inclusive and open dialogue with and between civil society organisations. More specifically, the action particularly addresses the call¿s specific objective to support civil society organisations in Jordan working on human rights (political, economic, social, and cultural), democratisation, good governance and development in Jordan. In addition, it will directly support achieving the call¿s sub-theme under lot 3: CSOs Coordination Mechanism for Sustainable Development.

The action will directly benefit 21 national and mid-level CSOs from 3 governorates targeted according to needs. The action will also benefit an estimated 42 CBOs through cascaded capacity building trainings provided by the national and mid-level CSOs targeted with institutional capacity building trainings and introduced to the Training of Trainer (ToT) tool developed under Activity 1.2.2 (2 for each of the 21 targeted CSOs). Notably, the action will target CSOs engaged in advocacy, policy dialogue/monitoring and/or community mobilisation in at least one of the subthemes related to sustainable development as defined by Acted¿s 3Zero strategy: a) human rights and governance; b) environmental sustainability and climate change; or c) economic cooperation, with a focus on inclusion, circular economy and migration (full selection criteria detailed under Activity 1.1.2).

Specifically, the project will approximately target 342 total female and male beneficiaries from the mid and national CSOs provided with institutional and technical capacity building training as follows: a) IRCHF and their employees (Acted will target approximately 6 IRC-KHF staff members), b) 21 CSO staff members and their managing board members (approximately 10 people per CSO6), c) 42 CBOs staff members (approximately 3 people per CBO) . The action will also indirectly target the wider populations of the three targeted governorates through the end goal of improved public services and efforts towards sustainable development as a result of enhancing CSOs and the overall civic spaces that enable inclusive, participatory, and collective engagement in policy making processes and public accountability.

In addition, the action will engage working groups including government institutions, national unions and private sector actors to facilitate comprehensive and integrated feedback into policy frameworks, thereby strengthening multi-stakeholder collaboration, as well as buy-in and support for CSO-led collection advocacy and public accountability initiatives.
